note: Answer key. Reviewers never see this file. A finding matches a flaw when it identifies the same defect and its consequence; naming the area without the defect does not count. Severity: major breaks a stated requirement or the service, minor is a real but smaller defect.

flaws.flaw: gateway.refund does not exist: src/services/gateway.js only exports charge, so the plan's central call fails.
flaws.must_say: the gateway client has no refund operation (only charge), so it must be added or the plan cannot work

flaws.flaw: voidInvoice moves a paid invoice to void, but ALLOWED lets only open invoices become void and a paid invoice is final, so the transition throws after the money is returned.
flaws.must_say: paid to void is not an allowed transition (paid is final); the plan needs a new refunded state or a changed transition table, and must order the gateway call and the status change safely

flaws.flaw: The guard is requireAuth plus assertCanRead, which lets the owning customer refund their own invoice; the requirement is admins only and the plan never calls requireAdmin.
flaws.must_say: authorisation permits the invoice's own customer to refund; it needs requireAdmin

flaws.flaw: GET /invoices changes from a bare array to an object with items, page, limit and total, which breaks every existing client, with no versioning or opt-in.
flaws.must_say: the response shape change breaks existing callers; keep the array by default or version it

flaws.flaw: page and limit are not validated: NaN, zero, negative or huge values give wrong slices or the whole table.
flaws.must_say: page and limit need validation and a maximum

flaws.flaw: The new test file is not added to the explicit test list in package.json, so npm test passes without running it and the verification is vacuous.
flaws.must_say: test/pagination.test.js is not in the package.json test script so npm test will not run it

flaws.flaw: The client address is taken from the client-controlled x-forwarded-for header, but the service has no reverse proxy (README), so an attacker sets a new value per request and never hits the limit.
flaws.must_say: x-forwarded-for is spoofable and there is no trusted proxy, so the limit can be bypassed

flaws.flaw: The per-address Map is never pruned, so entries (also spoofable keys) accumulate without bound.
flaws.must_say: the attempts map grows without eviction, a memory leak an attacker can drive

flaws.flaw: list() keeps only customers with deletedAt === null, but existing records have no deletedAt (undefined), so every existing customer disappears; the plan wrongly says no migration is needed.
flaws.must_say: existing customers lack deletedAt so a strict null check hides them all; treat missing as not deleted or migrate

flaws.flaw: customers.get still returns deleted customers, so invoices can still be created for a deleted customer (and their users keep working).
flaws.must_say: get and invoice creation do not respect deletedAt, so a deleted customer can still be invoiced

flaws.flaw: The overdue-reminder job looks customers up in the raw data and never checks deletedAt, so deleted customers keep getting reminder emails.
flaws.must_say: the reminders job still emails soft-deleted customers

p05.title: download an invoice as a PDF

flaws.flaw: Adds pdfkit as a runtime dependency and runs npm install, against the README rule of no runtime dependencies (deployed by copying the folder).
flaws.must_say: this violates the no-runtime-dependencies rule; render the PDF by hand or use another route

flaws.flaw: The handler authenticates but never calls assertCanRead, so any logged-in user can download any invoice by id.
flaws.must_say: no ownership check: any authenticated customer can fetch another customer's invoice PDF

p06.title: webhook when an invoice is paid

flaws.flaw: Receivers must be able to verify a call came from Ledgerly, but the plan has no signature, shared secret or HMAC.
flaws.must_say: no signing or shared secret, so the receiver cannot authenticate the call

flaws.flaw: Delivery, with up to three tries, 2 second pauses and no request timeout, runs inline in the pay path, so a slow or hanging receiver delays or hangs the customer's payment response.
flaws.must_say: delivery must be off the pay path or have a timeout; retries inline block the request

flaws.flaw: webhookUrl is accepted with no validation of scheme or host, so the server fetches any URL, including internal addresses.
flaws.must_say: the webhook URL is not validated (scheme, private or internal hosts)

p07.title: invoices in more than one currency

flaws.flaw: JPY has no minor unit, but the plan prints every currency with two decimals and treats totalCents as hundredths, so 1234 yen shows as 12.34 yen.
flaws.must_say: JPY is zero-decimal; the cents model and formatting are wrong for it

flaws.flaw: gateway.charge takes only amountCents and card and has no currency, so the plan's pass-through does nothing and a EUR or GBP invoice is charged as USD.
flaws.must_say: the gateway client has no currency parameter, so foreign invoices would be charged in the wrong currency

flaws.flaw: totalUsdCents is computed from a live external rate on every read of GET /invoices, with no fallback, so a rate-provider outage breaks reading invoices.
flaws.must_say: reads depend on an external service with no failure path; store the rate or degrade gracefully

flaws.flaw: Invoices stored before the change have no currency field and the plan does not default them, so formatting and the rate lookup receive undefined.
flaws.must_say: legacy invoices have no currency; missing must read as USD

p08.title: a persistent queue for overdue reminders

flaws.flaw: A job is claimed as running before the email is sent; if the process dies or email.send throws (it throws on a bad address) the job stays running forever, with no lease, timeout, retry or failed state, so the reminder is lost.
flaws.must_say: jobs stuck in running after a crash or send failure are never recovered

flaws.flaw: The scan does not skip invoices that already have a queued or running job and lastReminderAt is only written when the worker finishes, so each scan queues duplicates; the plan's own test (scan twice, then run the worker) would send two emails.
flaws.must_say: no dedupe of existing queued jobs, so repeated scans enqueue duplicate reminders

flaws.flaw: The worker does not re-read the invoice before sending, so an invoice paid or voided after it was queued still gets a reminder, against the acceptance criteria.
flaws.must_say: the invoice status must be rechecked when the job runs

p09.title: an audit log for admin actions

flaws.flaw: The record stores the raw request body, and an admin can call POST /invoices/:id/pay, whose body holds the card number and cvc, against the requirement that card data is never logged.
flaws.must_say: raw request bodies include card data on the pay route; redact or whitelist fields

flaws.flaw: The record is written only after a successful handler and failures are swallowed, so failed or partial admin actions and any write error leave the action unlogged, against the 'every admin action must be logged' requirement.
flaws.must_say: audit is best-effort and post-hoc: failed attempts and audit write failures are lost

flaws.flaw: The central handler in server.js never has the user: each route handler calls session.requireAuth itself and returns only status and body, so the hook has no user or role to test.
flaws.must_say: server.js has no authenticated user at that point; the hook cannot know the actor without re-authenticating or changing the handler contract

flaws.flaw: Sessions live in an in-memory Map, so a restart signs everyone out; the plan promises they survive a restart but adds no persistence.
flaws.must_say: sessions are in memory and are lost on restart, contradicting the acceptance criterion

flaws.flaw: Sliding renewal with no absolute maximum age and no logout or revocation lets a stolen token live indefinitely, and the lifetime is raised from 8 hours to 30 days.
flaws.must_say: sliding expiry needs an absolute cap and a way to revoke sessions

flaws.flaw: requireAuth receives only req and handlers return only status and body, so it cannot set the x-session-expires response header without changing the handler contract.
flaws.must_say: requireAuth has no access to the response, so the header cannot be set as planned
